scenes.name: Breakbeat hardcore: N-Joi y The Prodigy
scenes.book: Techno Rebels: The Renegades of Electronic Funk
scenes.author: Dan Sicko
scenes.desc: N-Joi (RCA, 1991) mezcló techno con montones de breakbeats sampleados («Let the bass kick», «Drop the bass now!») y entró en el terreno fronterizo con el hip hop que se llamó hardcore. Liam Howlett, antiguo DJ de «brit-hop», unió el breakbeat al house rápido; con What Evil Lurks (1990) fichó por XL con Leeroy Thornhill y el bailarín Keith Flint, y «Charly» fue número tres británico en 1991. Los ravers vieron en sus ritmos dispersos (y en sus muchos clones infantiles) un anatema contra el bombo a negras; Mixmag preguntó en portada en 1992: «¿Mató “Charly” al rave?». De esa división nacieron el jungle y el drum & bass. Prodigy triunfó en Estados Unidos con estética punk y Flint como cantante, en el sello Maverick de Madonna: The Fat of the Land (1997), con «Firestarter» y «Breathe», más de dos millones de copias.

podcast.title: Death and Estate Auction (2019)
podcast.body: Keith Flint, the dancer and singer for The Prodigy, took his own life on March 4, 2019. Despite owning a pub called The Leather Bottle, he was heavily in debt. Following his death, his possessions were auctioned off to settle his debts, raising a total of 350,000 pounds. Among the items sold was an unusual stuffed rabbit wearing a backpack and carrying a shotgun. "And among the items that were sold was a stuffed rabbit wearing a backpack and carrying a shotgun."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Keith Flint's Death in 2019
xref.body: Keith Flint of The Prodigy passed away in 2019, joining a growing list of deceased musicians. "Then in 2019, Keith Flynn of the Prodigy."

xref.title: Coping Mechanisms
xref.body: Boxing and jiu-jitsu were activities that helped Keith Flint manage his mental health issues, but ultimately proved insufficient to address his deeper struggles. "Boxing and jiu-jitsu helped, but it wasn't enough."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Coroner's Inquest Ambiguity on Suicide
xref.body: The coroner's inquest was unable to definitively determine whether Keith Flint's hanging was deliberate or accidental, despite the presence of codeine, alcohol, and a small amount of cocaine in his system. The inquest concluded, "Having regard to all the circumstances, I don't find there's enough evidence for suicide. He may have been walking around, and it all went horribly wrong." "The coroner's inquest was unable to determine if Keith's hanging was deliberate or an accident."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Discovery of Keith Flint's Death
xref.body: On March 4, 2019, police were called to Keith Flint's house for a welfare check and found him dead sometime before 9 p.m., at the age of 49. "On March 4, 2019, someone called police and asked for a welfare check at Keith's house."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind Blowing Facts in 60 Minutes: The 5th Edition

xref.title: Keith Flint's Fear of Flying
xref.body: Keith Flint suffered from a strong dislike of flying, which led to a reputation as a difficult passenger, including an incident where he attempted to kick in a cockpit door on a transatlantic flight and was removed from other flights for being deemed "unfit to fly." "He didn't like to fly and had a reputation as a difficult passenger."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Keith Flint's Home Life and Hobbies
xref.body: Keith Flint owned a house in the Essex countryside that included a small track for motorcycle riding, was filled with dogs, and had a pond that attracted birds, leading him to take up bird watching. He also owned and seemed to enjoy running a nearby pub. "The house was filled with dogs, and had a pond that attracted birds, and Keith got heavily into bird watching."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Keith Flint's Marital Status at Time of Death
xref.body: At the time of his death, Keith Flint was separated from his wife, although individuals were still "keeping tabs on him." "At the time he died, Keith was separated from his wife."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Keith Flint's Mental Health and Addictions
xref.body: Keith Flint struggled with depression and developed an addiction to prescription painkillers, in addition to engaging in heavy drinking. "He suffered from depression and became addicted to prescription painkillers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Keith Flint's Motorcycle Racing and Team
xref.body: Outside of music, Keith Flint was deeply involved in motorcycles and motorcycle racing, even owning his own team called Traction Control, which competed across the UK. "When he wasn't working on music, he was into motorcycles and motorcycle racing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Keith Flint's Role as Frontman
xref.body: Keith Flint was recognized as an "amazing frontman and dancer" for The Prodigy, characterized by his distinctive piercings, tattoos, and wild hair. "Keith made an amazing frontman and dancer with his piercings and tattoos and wild hair."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Keith Flint's Solo Band "Flint"
xref.body: Keith Flint maintained his own band, separate from The Prodigy, called Flint. "He also had his own band called Flint."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Liam Howlett's Announcement of Suicide
xref.body: Later on the day of Keith Flint's death, The Prodigy's leader, Liam Howlett, announced that Flint's death had been a suicide by hanging. "Later that day, prodigy leader Liam Howett announced that Keith's death had been a suicide. He'd hanged himself."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
